title: Foreign manpower and levy rules for hawkers and small F&B operators
asked: Whether more graduated or proportional foreign manpower arrangements and levy thresholds could be considered for hawkers and small food and beverage operators, so they can meet essential kitchen and service staffing needs while still ensuring fair wages and protections for all workers.
response: Hawker centre stallholders must be Singaporean Citizens or Permanent Residents under MSE rules, though stallholders can hire eligible Long-Term Visit Pass and Long-Term Visit Pass-Plus holders already in Singapore. Licensed food shops such as restaurants can hire foreign workers subject to the services levy and a quota of two locals to one foreign worker, and micro enterprises with only one local worker may hire a first Work Permit Holder. Dr Koh said differentiating levies and quotas further to favour smaller operators could push larger operators to break up into smaller entities and raise foreign worker numbers unsustainably. He pointed to the FoodX programme, the F&B Process Optimisation Programme and the Productivity Solutions Grant, and said MOM will continue to review foreign manpower policies for hawkers and small F&B companies with relevant agencies including MSE.

key_points.point: Hawker centre stallholders must be Singaporean Citizens or Permanent Residents, under MSE rules.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: only allows Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents to be stallholders at our hawker centres

key_points.point: Stallholders can hire eligible Long-Term Visit Pass and Long-Term Visit Pass-Plus holders who are already in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Stallholders can also hire eligible Long-Term Visit Pass and Long-Term Visit Pass-Plus holders

key_points.point: Licensed food shops like restaurants can hire foreign workers, subject to the services foreign worker levy rates and a quota of two locals to one foreign worker.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: subject to the services foreign worker levy rates and quota of two locals to one foreign worker

key_points.point: Micro enterprises with only one local worker may hire their first Work Permit Holder.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we allow those with only one local worker to hire their first Work Permit Holder

key_points.point: Differentiating levies and quotas further to favour smaller operators could lead larger operators to split into smaller entities to hire more foreign workers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: could incentivise the larger operators to break up into smaller entities to hire more foreign workers

key_points.point: Support schemes cited include the FoodX programme, which supports outsourcing labour-intensive food preparation to central kitchens.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the FoodX programme, which supports the outsourcing of labour-intensive food preparation to central kitchens to improve operational efficiency

key_points.point: MOM will continue to review foreign manpower policies for hawkers and small F&B companies with relevant agencies including MSE.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We will continue to review the foreign manpower policies for hawkers and small F&B companies

key_points.point: On giving smaller operators more headcount, MOM is agnostic if it makes sense at a certain productivity level.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon

key_points.point: Smaller operators may have to rethink their business model and use government resources such as central kitchens rather than relying on headcount.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: smaller operators may really also have to rethink their business model

left_open: Whether graduated or proportional levy thresholds will be introduced specifically for hawkers and small F&B operators.
Whether MOM will look at data on single operators and hawkers pushed into a higher Dependency Ratio Ceiling tier or exiting the business.
supplementary: Whether single-outlet hawkers and F&B operators pushed into a higher Dependency Ratio Ceiling tier can be helped, and whether MOM will study their data.
